label: first copy step (after <DEL>), weakly favoring first token 3/g and sequences rich in w/0/t
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.04% of steps). 99% of activation mass is in the copy phase, and 72% falls on the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, where the input is the echoed first token). It almost never fires in the original phase and never on the delimiter step. Within that step it fires on only 0.4% of sequences. It is enriched when the first token is 3 or g (lift 12x / 7x) and when the sequence contains w, 0 or t (as out_tok / next_out) or several digits, but none of these conditions is selective. The best predicates reach F1 ~0.06-0.12 (recall_idx==1 & in_tok in {3,g}: precision 0.03, recall 0.37). The top activations (3 followed by w/0-heavy sequences) suggest it depends on a conjunction of hidden-state contents that the available variables do not capture. Magnitude is fairly uniform (median 0.12, max 0.27); the largest values come from first-token-3 sequences containing w and 0.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=g (+4.68), prev_tok=h (+4.25), phase=2 & in_tok=3 (+3.79), phase=2 & in_tok=2 (+3.52), phase=2 & in_tok=h (+3.12), phase=2 & out_tok=t (+3.04).
